subject: Post-demo: Latency parity plan + hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@helixhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick latency question

Thanks for the demo earlier — good session. A couple of quick items we want to capture as we scope the POC:

- Can you summarize how Redwood compares to the hyperscalers for cross-region tail latency (us-east → eu-west) for 2k token prompts?
- We care about data residency: if we route requests from our EU customers to eu-west, can logs/telemetry ever leave that region?
- Procurement requested an initial cost estimate assuming 5k reqs/day at 1.5k tokens avg, plus notes on burst handling.

Appreciate a short write-up and any test artifacts we can run.

—Alex
Director, Platforms
Helix Health
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@helixhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick latency question

Alex — thanks, glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps and attached test plan.

1) Cross-region tail latency (2k tokens):
   - Hyperscaler A (managed endpoints): typically consistent p50/p90 but higher p99 on cold starts; we’ve seen ~120–180ms delta vs in-region for p99 on similar workloads.
   - Hyperscaler B (VM-backed endpoints): lower median but more variance under burst.
   - Redwood: we focus on routing + lightweight model variants and KV prefix caching to reduce cross-region p99. Based on prior customer tests we often see 30–80ms lower p99 vs Hyperscaler A when using eu-local cache + us-edge routing, and better consistent throttling for bursts.

2) Data residency:
   - For Private/Dedicated customers we can ensure logs and telemetry are stored in-region (eu-west). Hosted customers can opt into regional residency; telemetry can be configured to never leave the VPC or to be forwarded only to a customer-controlled KMS.

3) Cost estimate: attaching a simple cost model for your traffic profile — see redwood_test-plan-20261012.pdf. Short estimate: ~$1.6k/mo for steady 5k reqs/day at 1.5k tokens (hosted, standard model) before discounts; Dedicated committed pricing reduces unit cost materially.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marcus to run a 48-hour cross-region parity test (us-east ↔ eu-west) using your sample prompt set — output will include p50/p90/p99 and token-level breakdown. (Marcus: can you kick this off tomorrow?)
- Neha to send a short data-residency addendum we can include in the SOW.
- Alex to share a small prompt corpus and confirm IP/PII redaction rules.

Attaching: redwood_test-plan-20261012.pdf (test plan + cost model).

Cheers,
Laura
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@helixhealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick latency question

Alex — I kicked off the parity test this morning against eu-west and us-east with your corpus (sanitized sample). Quick notes:

- Test configuration: 2 concurrent workers per region, 2k token limit, 100ms think time to simulate interactive bursts.
- Models: Redwood standard-1 (quantized runtime), HyperscalerA-gen (managed), HyperscalerB-vm (provisioned).
- What we'll capture: p50/p90/p99, cold start distribution, token-level CPU/GPU breakdown, and request routing map.

I'll upload raw results and a first-pass csv in ~36 hrs. For now, we see median parity across regions but p99 gap favoring Redwood when the local KV cache is applied.

Attachments: latency-results-us-eu-raw.csv (preliminary).

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@helixhealth.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick latency question

Thanks Marcus — quick clarifying Qs as we prep procurement:

1) Are the p99 improvements you mentioned observable without custom quantization? We need something that works with models we already host.
2) For the residency addendum: can you confirm the retention window for request logs if we choose eu-only telemetry? Procurement needs a number.
3) Can we get a short one-pager that summarizes the failover behavior if a region becomes unavailable (routing, fallback models, SLA impact)?

If you can get answers by EOD today, procurement can draft the initial contract language.

—Alex
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@helixhealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick latency question

Alex — answers inline and docs attached.

1) p99 improvements without custom quantization: yes. Our routing + prefix/KV caching yields lower p99 for repeated patterns and system prompts even on standard quantized models. If you want further gains we can recommend a minimal quantization profile (no model code changes on your side).

2) Retention window: for eu-only telemetry we offer 90 days by default; can be configured to 30/90/365 per SOW. Logs never leave the configured region for Private/Dedicated; hosted customers can elect region-lock and KMS.

3) Failover behavior one-pager: attached (redwood_failover-onepager-20261014.pdf). TL;DR: automatic region routing with canary fallback to nearest compatible model variant; SLA impact depends on capacity tier — Dedicated customers have reserved capacity and defined RTO/RPO in the SOW.

I'll loop in Security for any follow-up evidence (SOC2 artifact) if procurement requests.

—Neha
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
